methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $15M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Foundry Lab is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $15M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private companies and one public company in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including later-stage peers such as Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and earlier-stage reference points like Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $15M total raised as a baseline and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $30M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range spanning $1.1B to $1.8B. The wide dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity in the comp set, with two Series B valuations and one Seed valuation.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $26M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $840M. The wide band reflects material uncertainty about whether Foundry Lab's current positioning is more appropriately benchmarked to near-term peers or to the broader cohort of robotics firms. Stage-progression implies sub-$50M valuation; peer-median implies multibillion-dollar territory. Key uncertainties include the company's technology differentiation relative to the comp set and its nearness to Series B fundraising.
